To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sugammadex is safe when dosed according to ideal body weight (ibw) and that it can reverse neuromus-cular blockade (NMB), as measured by accelerromyography, in patients who are morbidly obese.

the use of IBW for sugammadex administration is associated with a higher incidence of inadequate reversal of NMB and with higher plasma concentrations of sugammadex than those observed when using actual body weight (ABW).
sugammadex administered to reverse NMB at the reappearance or second twitch of TOF stimulation is safe and effective in patients who have undergone bariatric surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a single dose of sugammadex on post-operative recovery in morbidly obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery.
the effects of a single dose of sugammadex on the recovery of NMB after rocuronium administration.
the effects of the use of sugammadex at doses of 2 and 4 mg/kg on the reversal of NMB at the reappearance and disappearance of the TOF in patients undergoing bariatric surgery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that sugammadex is a safe and efficacious agent for reversal of rocuronium NMB at the reappearance (or not) of second twitch during TOF stimulation.
there is no clear evidence that the use of sugammadex in obese patients is safe and effective.
the use of sugammadex at IBW to reverse neuromu- scular block in bariatric surgery is safe but may be less effective than at total body weight (TBW).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are not sure if the dose of sugammadex based on IBW is as effective as that based on total body weight (TBW) in reversing neuromuscular block (NMB) in morbidly obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery.
the use of sugammadex at a dose of 4 mg kg\({}^{-1}\) IBW is effective and safe in reversing NMB in morbidly obese patients.
sugammadex is safe and effective when administered on the basis on IBW to reverse NMB in patients with BMI > 30 kg/m2 undergoing bariatric surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the administration of sugammadex based on IBW is safe and effective.
, in the absence of a reliable method for estimating the volume of distribution of sugammadex, a dose based on IBW is not a safe approach to reverse NMB in bariatric patients.
